reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a tutorial and promotional overview of uploading and selling photographs through a named stock-photography platform, including its submission workflow and referral feature. Although it describes revenue-share, referral, and high-volume contribution benefits, the sampled account pages show no listed photo earnings, referral signups, or credited amount, so the claims remain unverified without establishing deceptive conduct or a completed payment outcome.

citations.quote: In this video, I am sharing how you can sell photos online & make a lot of money.
I'll tell you how you'll upload photos what kind of review process is all about everything.
First upload photos from some options here.
every time you share your link with someone you get 10 rupees in your account
Create your account & earn Rs. 50 immediately

opening.argument: Judge, the offer asks viewers to take a specific action for an immediate cash reward: create an account through the supplied signup link or use the supplied code. The same pitch says stock photography can earn more than Rs. 1,00,000 per month. That pairing matters. The viewer is given a route to participate before any sale or payout is demonstrated, so this is more than a general discussion of photography income.

citations.quote: Create your account & earn Rs. 50 immediately - https://upload.picxy.com/signup/?ref=HXIYYPI or Use my code - HXIYYPI
You can earn more than Rs. 1,00,000 per month by doing stock photography.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The upload walkthrough explains what a participant would do after joining; it does not establish that the advertised immediate reward is credited. The referral feature likewise reinforces the solicitation: sharing a link is expressly tied to money in the account. The absence of credited earnings should make the judge cautious about treating the promised return as verified.

citations.quote: every time you share your link with someone you get 10 rupees in your account

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited invitation and earnings claims are promotional, but neither shows that the reward is false or that a viewer loses money. The video also demonstrates an ordinary contributor workflow: selecting photos, entering details and sending them for review. The visible earnings and referral pages do not show a completed payout, but that absence does not establish deception either.

opening.argument: Judge, assess the claims together: the description offers an immediate signup reward, a monthly income exceeding Rs. 1,00,000, and income earned even while sleeping. The speaker adds a bonus for uploading 500 or more photos at once. Those promises make a substantial return sound accessible through straightforward participation, while the cited claims themselves provide no example of a completed sale or payment. That gap is material when the pitch is asking viewers to commit their photos and time.

citations.quote: Create your account & earn Rs. 50 immediately
You can earn more than Rs. 1,00,000 per month by doing stock photography.
The money you earn through Stock Photography is a passive income, which you can make even when you are sleeping.
You upload 500 or more photos at once on the website, you get a fix, you get a price, an extra that will be a bonus for you

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense points to submission steps and empty account pages as though they neutralize the income pitch. Submission steps show how to enter the offer, not whether the advertised returns are attainable. An earnings page without listed sales cannot substantiate the monthly or passive-income claims; it leaves the most consequential part of the pitch untested.

citations.quote: You can earn more than Rs. 1,00,000 per month by doing stock photography.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are strong income claims, but the video does not present them as guaranteed earnings for every signup. The platform page describes revenue share and earnings on photo sales, and the walkthrough shows photos being prepared for review. No completed payout is shown, yet an unverified promotional claim is not, by itself, evidence of a deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: You can earn more than Rs. 1,00,000 per month by doing stock photography.

opening.argument: Judge, the screen demonstration should be read alongside the call to participate. The description gives viewers a signup link and the speaker's code; the presentation displays that code beside prompts to sell photos and make referral income. Later, the speaker describes a payment for sharing a referral link. The tutorial supplies the steps for entering the promoted platform, but its practical detail also makes the account-creation and referral pitch more persuasive. The central viewer-facing invitation remains: join through the supplied route and pursue the advertised rewards.

citations.quote: every time you share your link with someone you get 10 rupees in your account

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately identifies a photo-upload demonstration, but that does not make the video merely instructional. The description directs viewers to create an account for an immediate reward, and the speaker explicitly explains referral income. Those invitations are part of what the demonstration is promoting; showing a real interface does not verify the promised credits or earnings.

citations.quote: Create your account & earn Rs. 50 immediately
Then you have an amazing option of making referral income. by sharing your code or your referral link

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The video is promotional as well as instructional, but promotion is not itself evidence of a scam. The speaker walks through photo submission, and the visible referral page describes a single signup reward while showing no credited referrals. The prosecution's citations establish an invitation to use the platform, not a fabricated platform, a false payment, or a deceptive outcome.
